speeches.speaker: Sussan Ley
speeches.brief: The Morrison government introduced the first tranche of reforms to the Environment Protection and Biodiversity Conservation Act, moving to streamline environmental approvals by removing duplication with states and territories through a single-touch approval system agreed by national cabinet on 24 July 2020. The bill enables approval bilateral agreements with states and territories, following an independent review led by Professor Graeme Samuel, with his final recommendations due in October.

speeches.speaker: Terri Butler
speeches.brief: The speaker moved an amendment to decline the Environment Protection and Biodiversity Conservation Amendment (Streamlining Environmental Approvals) Bill 2020, arguing it ignores the Samuel Review's recommendations, fails to protect the environment or create jobs, and cited a 510% blowout in approval times and 79% of approval decisions affected by error due to government funding cuts.

speeches.speaker: Joel Fitzgibbon
speeches.brief: The opposition rejected the Environment Protection and Biodiversity Conservation Amendment (Streamlining Environmental Approvals) Bill 2020 as premature, arguing the Samuel review found the EPBC Act serves neither the environment nor industry, and that the government failed to make a coherent case for the bill. The speaker also noted a $34 million stewardship package announced in March 2019 has not yet commenced, with programs not starting until 2021.

speeches.speaker: Matt Keogh
speeches.brief: The speaker argued that the Morrison government's cuts to the environment department have caused a 510% increase in approval delays and that the proposed bill ignores the Samuel review's recommendations for national environmental standards, failing both jobs and the environment. Labor will not support the bill and will refer it to a Senate committee inquiry.

speeches.speaker: Matt Thistlethwaite
speeches.brief: The speaker opposed the Environment Protection and Biodiversity Conservation Amendment (Streamlining Environmental Approvals) Bill 2020, arguing it would weaken federal environmental protections by devolving approvals to states and ignoring key recommendations from Graeme Samuel’s independent review, including the establishment of national environmental standards. The speaker cited a 510% increase in average approval delays since 2014, 75% of decisions containing errors, and Australia’s highest mammal extinction rate, and called for a national environmental watchdog.

speeches.speaker: Josh Burns
speeches.brief: The Labor Party opposed the Environment Protection and Biodiversity Conservation Amendment (Streamlining Environmental Approvals) Bill 2020, arguing it would weaken environmental protections, reduce transparency, and cede federal oversight to the states. The speaker criticised the government for ignoring the Samuel review’s recommendations, including establishing strong national environmental standards and an independent environmental protection agency, and noted that no coalition member spoke in support of the bill.

speeches.speaker: Adam Bandt
speeches.brief: The speaker argued that the Morrison government's Environment Protection and Biodiversity Conservation Amendment (Streamlining Environmental Approvals) Bill 2020 would weaken federal environmental protections by handing approval powers to states, citing risks to wildlife and heritage sites like Juukan Gorge, and criticised the government for ignoring its own independent review's call for stronger national standards and an independent regulator.

speeches.speaker: Tony Burke
speeches.brief: The member moved to suspend standing orders to allow all members wishing to speak on the Environment Protection and Biodiversity Conservation Amendment (Streamlining Environmental Approvals) Bill 2020 to do so, arguing that the bill rehashes a failed Abbott-era proposal and contradicts the government-commissioned Samuel Review interim report.
